conceptCapsule.title: Moment of a Force (Torque) & Equilibrium
conceptCapsule.summary: 1. Definition: Torque (moment of a force) about a reference point $O$ is defined as $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$, where $\vec{r}$ is the position vector of the point of application of force relative to $O$. 2. Magnitude & Lever Arm: $|\vec{\tau}| = r F \sin\theta = F \cdot r_\perp = r \cdot F_\perp$, where $r_\perp$ is the perpendicular distance (lever arm) from the pivot to the line of action of the force. 3. Couple: Two equal, opposite, and non-collinear parallel forces form a couple whose torque is independent of the reference origin: $\tau = F \cdot d_\perp$. 4. Principle of Moments: For rotational equilibrium of a rigid body, $\sum \vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$ (sum of clockwise moments equals sum of counter-clockwise moments). 5. Conservation Link: $\vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\vec{L}}{dt}$; if $\vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$, angular momentum $\vec{L}$ remains strictly conserved.
conceptCapsule.examTrap: Torque is always defined relative to a specific reference point or axis. The cross product order $\vec{r} \times \vec{F}$ is crucial; writing $\vec{F} \times \vec{r}$ yields the opposite vector direction ($-\vec{\tau}$). Additionally, remember that internal forces between particles in a rigid body exert zero net internal torque.

questions.statement: A force $\vec{F} = (2\hat{i} - 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k})\text{ N}$ acts at a point whose position vector is $\vec{r} = (3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k})\text{ m}$. The torque $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$ about the origin is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 3 & 2 & 3 \\ 2 & -3 & 4 \end{vmatrix} = \hat{i}(8 - (-9)) - \hat{j}(12 - 6) + \hat{k}(-9 - 4) = 17\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} - 13\hat{k}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is projected with speed $u$ at an angle $	heta$ to the horizontal from the origin $(0, 0)$. The magnitude of torque of the gravitational force on the projectile about the launch point when it reaches its maximum height is:
questions.solution:
At maximum height, the horizontal position is $x = \frac{R}{2} = \frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{2g}$.
The perpendicular distance from the launch point to the line of action of gravity ($F_g = mg$) is $r_\perp = x$.
$$\tau = F_g \cdot x = (mg)\left(\frac{u^2 \sin 2\theta}{2g}\right) = \frac{m u^2 \sin 2\theta}{2}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: The torque $\vec{\tau}$ acting on a body about a reference point $O$ is always:
questions.solution:
By the definition of the vector cross product, $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}$ is perpendicular to both the position vector $\vec{r}$ and the force vector $\vec{F}$ ($\vec{\tau} \cdot \vec{r} = 0$, $\vec{\tau} \cdot \vec{F} = 0$).
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A uniform rod $AB$ of length $L = 2\text{ m}$ is hinged at end $A$. A force $F = 50\text{ N}$ acts at end $B$ making an angle of $30^\circ$ with the rod. The magnitude of the torque exerted by this force about the hinge $A$ is:
questions.solution:
$$\tau = r F \sin\phi = (2\text{ m})(50\text{ N})\sin 30^\circ = 100 \times \frac{1}{2} = 50\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A particle moves in the $xy$-plane along the straight line $y = 4\text{ m}$ with a constant velocity $\vec{v} = (5\hat{i})\text{ m/s}$. If the mass of the particle is $m = 2\text{ kg}$ and a constant force $\vec{F} = (6\hat{i})\text{ N}$ acts on it, the torque of the force about the origin is:
questions.solution:
Position vector is $\vec{r} = x\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}\text{ m}$. Force is $\vec{F} = 6\hat{i}\text{ N}$.
$$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = (x\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}) \times (6\hat{i}) = 24(\hat{j} \times \hat{i}) = -24\hat{k}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A force $\vec{F} = (a\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 6\hat{k})\text{ N}$ acts at a point $\vec{r} = (2\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} - 12\hat{k})\text{ m}$. The value of constant $a$ for which the torque about the origin is strictly zero is:
questions.solution:
For $\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F} = \vec{0}$, the vectors $\vec{r}$ and $\vec{F}$ must be collinear:
$$\frac{2}{a} = \frac{-6}{3} = \frac{-12}{6} = -2 \implies a = -1$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: Two equal and opposite parallel forces of magnitude $F = 20\text{ N}$ act on the rim of a circular steering wheel of radius $R = 0.25\text{ m}$ to form a couple. The torque of this couple about any arbitrary point in the plane of the wheel is:
questions.solution:
The torque of a couple is independent of the reference origin and equals the force times perpendicular separation:
$$\tau = F(2R) = 20 \times (2 \times 0.25) = 20 \times 0.5 = 10\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A force $\vec{F} = 4\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}\text{ N}$ acts on a particle located at point $P(2, 3)	ext{ m}$. The torque of this force about the point $Q(1, 1)	ext{ m}$ is:
questions.solution:
Position vector of $P$ relative to $Q$: $\vec{r}_{P/Q} = (2 - 1)\hat{i} + (3 - 1)\hat{j} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j}\text{ m}$.
$$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r}_{P/Q} \times \vec{F} = (\hat{i} + 2\hat{j}) \times (4\hat{i} + 5\hat{j}) = (5 - 8)\hat{k} = -3\hat{k}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A uniform meter stick of mass $M = 0.6\text{ kg}$ is balanced horizontally on a knife-edge placed at the $40\text{ cm}$ mark when a mass $m$ is suspended at the $10\text{ cm}$ mark. The value of mass $m$ is:
questions.solution:
Meter stick weight acts at $50\text{ cm}$ (lever arm $= 50 - 40 = 10\text{ cm}$).
Suspended mass $m$ is at $10\text{ cm}$ (lever arm $= 40 - 10 = 30\text{ cm}$).
Torque equilibrium: $$m g (30) = M g (10) \implies m = \frac{0.6 \times 10}{30} = 0.2\text{ kg}$$
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is dropped from rest from a height $h$ at horizontal distance $d$ from the origin. The magnitude of torque of the gravitational force about the origin as a function of time $t$ until it lands is:
questions.solution:
The vertical line of action of gravity ($F = mg$) remains at a constant perpendicular distance $d$ from the origin throughout the fall: $$\tau = F \cdot r_\perp = m g d$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A solid circular disc of radius $R = 0.5\text{ m}$ has three tangential forces acting along its rim: $F_1 = 10\text{ N}$ (clockwise), $F_2 = 25\text{ N}$ (counter-clockwise), and $F_3 = 5\text{ N}$ (clockwise). The net torque acting on the disc about its central axle is:
questions.solution:
$$\tau_{\text{net}} = (F_2 - F_1 - F_3)R = (25 - 10 - 5)(0.5) = (10)(0.5) = 5.0\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}\text{ (counter-clockwise)}$$
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: The physical dimensions of torque are identical to the physical dimensions of:
questions.solution:
$$[\tau] = [r][F] = [\text{L}][\text{M L T}^{-2}] = [\text{M L}^2 \text{T}^{-2}]$$
This matches the dimensional formula for work and energy.
Therefore, Option B is correct.

questions.statement: A rectangular plate of sides $a = 0.4\text{ m}$ and $b = 0.3\text{ m}$ lies in the $xy$-plane with one corner at the origin. A force $\vec{F} = (10\hat{i} + 20\hat{j})\text{ N}$ is applied at the opposite diagonal corner $(a, b)$. The torque of this force about the origin is:
questions.solution:
$$\vec{\tau} = (0.4\hat{i} + 0.3\hat{j}) \times (10\hat{i} + 20\hat{j}) = (0.4 \times 20 - 0.3 \times 10)\hat{k} = (8 - 3)\hat{k} = +5.0\hat{k}\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A light horizontal rod $AB$ of length $L$ is pivoted at end $A$. Two forces $F_1$ and $F_2$ act perpendicularly to the rod at distances $L/3$ and $L$ respectively from $A$ in opposite senses. For rotational equilibrium ($\tau_{\text{net}} = 0$), the ratio $F_1 / F_2$ must be:
questions.solution:
$$F_1\left(\frac{L}{3}\right) - F_2(L) = 0 \implies \frac{F_1}{3} = F_2 \implies \frac{F_1}{F_2} = \frac{3}{1}$$
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: If the net torque acting on a system of particles about a point is zero ($\vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$), which of the following physical quantities must remain conserved about that point?
questions.solution:
From Newton's rotational second law, $\vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \frac{d\vec{L}}{dt}$. When $\vec{\tau}_{\text{ext}} = \vec{0}$, total angular momentum $\vec{L}$ is conserved.
Therefore, Option C is correct.

questions.statement: A uniform square lamina $ABCD$ of side length $a = 1\text{ m}$ is acted upon by forces $10\text{ N}, 20\text{ N}, 30\text{ N},$ and $40\text{ N}$ along the sides $AB, BC, CD,$ and $DA$ respectively in cyclic order. The magnitude of the net torque about the intersection of the diagonals is:
questions.solution:
Perpendicular lever arm distance from center to all sides is $r_\perp = a/2 = 0.5\text{ m}$.
$$\tau_{\text{net}} = (10 + 20 + 30 + 40)(0.5) = (100)(0.5) = 50\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A heavy door of width $W = 1.2\text{ m}$ is pushed with a force $F = 40\text{ N}$ applied at the outer handle perpendicular to the door surface. If the same torque is to be produced by pushing at a point $0.3\text{ m}$ from the hinges, the required perpendicular force is:
questions.solution:
$$\tau = F_1 W = 40 \times 1.2 = 48\text{ N}\cdot\text{m} \implies F_2 = \frac{\tau}{d} = \frac{48}{0.3} = 160\text{ N}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: A force $\vec{F} = (2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j})\text{ N}$ acts along the line $3x - 2y = 6$. The perpendicular lever arm distance $r_\perp$ of the line of action of the force from the origin is:
questions.solution:
$$r_\perp = \frac{|3(0) - 2(0) - 6|}{\sqrt{3^2 + (-2)^2}} = \frac{6}{\sqrt{13}}\text{ m}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.

questions.statement: Under which of the following conditions is the moment of a force (torque) about an axis strictly ZERO?

options.text: The line of action of the force intersects the axis of rotation
The line of action of the force is parallel to the axis of rotation
The magnitude of the force is zero

questions.solution:
Torque about an axis vanishes when $F = 0$, when the force intersects the axis ($r_\perp = 0$), or when the force is parallel to the axis.
Therefore, Option D is correct.

questions.statement: A particle of mass $m$ is executing uniform circular motion of radius $R$ with constant angular speed $\omega$ in the $xy$-plane centered at the origin. The net torque acting on the particle about the origin is:
questions.solution:
Centripetal force is directed radially inward towards the origin ($\vec{F}_c \parallel -\vec{r}$).
$$\vec{\tau} = \vec{r} \times \vec{F}_c = \vec{r} \times (-m\omega^2\vec{r}) = \vec{0}$$
Therefore, Option A is correct.
